decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach, rotate open grippers toward downward grasps while raising above the objects; estimate positions from head RGB.
Previous action rejected before motion; halve increments to preserve joint continuity while beginning downward orientation.
Continue turning downward; left approaches rear yellow car and right approaches nearby red pepper, staying in separate workspaces.
Finish vertical alignment and descend cautiously over the yellow car and right pepper; fingertip offset and grasp depth remain visually estimated.
Use wrist views to center the first car and pepper, lower another 3.5 cm, then close both grippers for a test lift.
Lift vertically with grippers closed to verify both objects remain between the fingers before moving toward baskets.
RGB shows both objects lifted. Carry yellow car over left basket and pepper over right basket, keeping closed and clear of rims.
Replan smaller increments after guard. Car appears to have slipped near left basket; reopen and approach it again while lowering the retained pepper over right basket.
Release pepper inside right basket. Recenter left fingers around the yellow car now on the table and close for another pickup.
Lift the regrasped car with closed left gripper; right clears the basket and approaches the rightmost chocolate wrapper.
Rejected motion executed nothing. Retreat right arm with very small initial steps away from its tight basket configuration; lift left car without opening.
Car visibly retained after regrasp. Carry it slowly into the left basket while right descends toward the rightmost chocolate bar.
Car slipped at the basket rim, so return for a deeper grasp and plan greater lift. Rotate right fingers across the chocolate bar's short dimension.
Back left fingers clear of the basket wall before descending. Continue right bar alignment and controlled descent with open fingers.
Regrasp car lower with vertical fingers. Recenter right bar grasp away from the neighboring white car and correct tilt using smaller increments after the rejection.
Adjust first right increment slightly toward its preceding accepted target to satisfy continuity; no prior rejected motion was executed.
Close on the centered bar at the current contact height rather than pushing lower. Lift both closed grippers vertically to verify retention and gain rim clearance.
Raise the retained car farther and tilt slightly forward to clear the left basket rim without extending the EE too far. Bar was not lifted; reopen and shift forward for regrasp.
Advance the securely held car fully beyond the left basket rim and release. Refine right bar centering and close at the lower grasp height.
First car is inside left basket. Approach remaining small yellow car with left arm; test-lift the right chocolate bar before transporting.
Bar fell back onto table and rotated; align fingers across its new short axis. Align left fingers across the small car and descend with both open.
Use wrist image offsets to center the car and chocolate between the fingers; descend only to the estimated tabletop grasp level and close.
Lift both closed grasps well above basket-rim height; gradually undo the left yaw only after initial clearance and verify both objects remain attached.
Both objects remain visibly held. Carry car toward left basket and chocolate toward the right side of the middle basket, keeping elevated and gently tilting forward for clearance.
After continuity interruption, use smaller inward/forward increments and slightly lower the right wrist. Release only after reaching the interiors of left and middle baskets.
Use millimeter-scale correction after guard: lower right wrist to relax its tight configuration and release the bar inside middle basket; release second car inside left basket.
Two cars and one chocolate now visibly in their baskets. Withdraw and approach remaining center chocolate with left and purple chocolate with right, restoring downward orientation.
Initial withdrawal rejected; reduce the first right-arm step from the tight basket pose, then continue separate approaches to the remaining chocolates.
Align each gripper across its chocolate bar's short dimension and descend toward the previously successful bar grasp height, staying on each arm's side.
Compensate the rotated link6-to-finger offset to center the left bar without crossing arms. Make a small right centering correction and close both at current contact height.
Lift the right purple chocolate to test retention. Left bar lies outside the closed fingers; reopen and correct mostly backward in world y with yaw held fixed, then reclose.
Neither chocolate retained. Clear and reorient left above the displaced bar. Reapproach the purple bar farther forward and lower to improve side engagement rather than pinching its upper edge.
Bring the purple bar toward the distal gripping region rather than the palm and close. Reorient and lower the left wrist above the red-and-white chocolate's new direction.
Test a straight vertical lift of the better-centered purple bar. Lower and close left fingers on the narrow white-and-red bar, then begin a small test lift without changing yaw.
Both bars now remain visibly between fingers during lifting. Raise and carry them toward separate sides of the middle basket with modest forward tilt and closed grippers.
Purple bar is retained; place it inside middle basket with a small forward-lowering motion. Left bar slipped onto the table; reopen and return above its updated pose.
Recenter left bar and correct residual tilt for deeper side contact. Withdraw right slowly from the tight basket configuration, then approach the remaining white car.
Reduce right withdrawal increments after the rejected step. Finish centering and closing on the left bar while bringing right above the white car.
Test a straight lift of the centered red-white bar without changing its orientation. Lower right fingers around the white car and close.
Carry the retained final chocolate toward the middle basket with clearance. Lift the white car on its own side, preparing a central tabletop transfer rather than crossing arms.

Final narrow chocolate slipped near the rim; leave it visible for a higher-clearance regrasp. Move left toward remaining pepper and carry white car to a central tabletop staging area without crossing arms.
Rejected action moved neither arm. Start left retreat with smaller increments to relax the basket-side configuration, then continue separate pepper approach and car staging.
Center and grasp the remaining left pepper. Lower and release the white car near the centerline for later left-arm retrieval, keeping right link6 on its own side.
Pepper moved left instead of being retained. Reopen, clear upward, and approach its new position; withdraw right arm away from the staged car to leave the centerline clear.
Refine pepper grasp using its visible wrist offset and close lower around its body. Hold right clear on its side, ready for the subsequent centerline transfer.
Lift pepper clear before moving inward toward a central staging area. Right stays clear and restores a forward-facing grasp orientation.
Pepper remains securely held. Carry it toward a centerline tabletop staging point while the right arm waits with clearance; do not cross the arms.
Lower pepper onto the centerline staging area with a slight inward finger tilt while keeping left link6 on the left; release before the right arm approaches.
Separate along depth for the staged transfers: left withdraws backward above the white car while right approaches the pepper after left has cleared.
Use separate front/back staging positions to grasp the white car with left and pepper with right; center from wrist views and keep both link6 positions on their own sides.
Test-lift the white car and move leftward clear of the transfer area. Pepper shifted behind right fingertips; reopen, rise, and recenter backward before another grasp.
White car is retained after transfer. Carry it toward left basket with rim clearance; lower right fingers around the now-centered pepper and close.
Move white car fully over the left basket before opening. Test-lift the pepper vertically, then carry it outward in the right workspace while closed.
Three cars are visible in the left basket. Carry the retained second pepper to the right basket while left returns above the red-white chocolate lying just in front of the middle basket.
Place second pepper fully inside the right basket and release. Correct left gripper tilt while descending above the remaining chocolate, watching clearance from the middle basket rim.
Both peppers are in the right basket. Withdraw and begin resetting right arm. Left backs away from the rim with a narrower opening before reapproaching the last bar.
Previous motion rejected without execution. Ramp the right retreat more gently from its basket pose; left continues its narrower, rim-clear approach.
Advance the narrower left grasp toward the bar without entering the basket wall, then close. Return right toward its observed starting pose with continuous small rotations.
Left closed beside the bar rather than on it. Lift clear and align across its actual short axis with a narrow opening. Finish right reset using smaller increments after the continuity rejection.
Bar is now centered between narrowly opened fingers with clearance from the basket wall. Descend vertically and close; keep right at its reset pose.
Basket interference prevents the vertical grasp from reaching the bar. Back the wrist away and tilt fingertips forward to reach the bar while keeping the palm clear of the rim.
Move the narrow tilted grasp off the basket wall and onto the visible bar, then descend and close. Right remains reset and open.
The bar is centered but the tilted fingertips closed above it. Reopen narrowly and lower three centimeters before closing; keep the cleared wrist approach and right reset pose.
The bar shifted outside the closed fingers. Reopen and move the tilted grasp toward its center rather than its end, with a small clearance lift before reclosing.
Bar rotated and moved away from the rim rather than being grasped. Clear upward and reorient for a fresh top-down grasp on its updated direction; keep right reset.
Clear the left wrist sideways for an unobstructed head view of the final bar and restore a vertical approach; repeated rim-side grasps have not retained it.
The unobstructed view shows the final bar diagonally on the table, clear of the rim. Approach its center with vertical fingers aligned across its short axis.
Advance along the bar toward its middle, compensating the link6-to-finger offset seen in the wrist view. Lower to the successful bar-grasp height and close narrowly.
The bar is centered in the closed fingers. Lift vertically without rotation to verify retention and clear the basket rim before transport.
The bar was not retained; reopen and approach its updated center again with slightly deeper side engagement and refined yaw, now clear of the basket rim.
Recenter the bar slightly left between the pads, close at contact height, and start a slow test lift to reduce slipping.
Continue a slow straight lift of the centered bar with the gripper fully commanded closed; verify sustained retention before changing orientation or moving over the basket.
The thin bar slipped again. Reopen and move the palm away from the rim while tilting fingers forward, allowing a deeper side grasp without pushing the wrist against the basket.
The tilted fingers now straddle the bar with the palm clear. Make a small centering correction, close lower on its sides, and test a short slow lift.
Keep the deeper tilted grasp closed and lift straight up slowly to check retention before attempting the final basket placement.
The deeper tilted grasp now retains the bar throughout lifting. Raise it above rim height and move gently toward the middle basket without changing the grasp orientation.
Carry the retained final bar farther into the middle basket. Lower the wrist gradually to maintain configuration margin while preserving clearance above the front rim.
Make a final millimeter-scale forward/lower adjustment with the bar over the middle basket, then release and allow it to settle. Right remains at origin.
The forward suffix was rejected, but the bar is already over the basket interior. Release at the observed pose, then withdraw with very small initial steps to relax the tight configuration.
Final bar is visibly inside the middle basket. Reduce the first withdrawal to submillimeter increments after rejection, then gradually retreat and begin returning the left arm to origin.
Replan from the latest pose after only two retreat steps executed. Use uniformly tiny backward/downward motions and gentle wrist rotation to relax the near-limit configuration without a joint jump.
Only one prior step executed. Hold orientation fixed and use finer radial retreat increments across the near-extension region before gradually increasing withdrawal.
The fine retreat cleared the near-extension region. Return the open left arm toward its observed origin with continuous elbow-up motion and gradual orientation restoration; right stays reset.
Only three prior steps executed. Use uniformly smaller retreat and rotation increments to continue the left reset; also correct the right arm's small accumulated origin residual.
Continue the open left arm along a gentle return toward its recorded origin, preserving joint continuity. All objects remain visibly in their category baskets; right stays at origin.
Approach the left origin with tapered increments near the final configuration, both grippers open. Make only tiny right-origin corrections while leaving the sorted baskets undisturbed.
